title: Executive Turntable: SiriusXM Names Jenny Tartikoff Senior VP & Head of Communications
summary: This week's column features the launch of Andrew Kautz's Kautz & Associates, Allen Mitchell's Reverie Ranch Group & more music industry hires and promotions.
contentText:
SiriusXM has named Jenny Tartikoff the company’s new senior vp and head of communications, effective on Monday, Aug. 10. She will report to Scott Greenstein , the company’s president and chief content officer. In her new role, Tartikoff will oversee SiriusXM’s content and serve as an advisor to its leadership team.

Tartikoff joins SiriusXM from Paramount Pictures, where she served as executive vp of global communications. Prior to that, she was head of content and advertising communications at Spotify and had been senior vp of global communications at Universal Filmed Entertainment Group. At the beginning of her career, she worked in communication for broadcast journalism, working at NBC News.

“Jenny is an accomplished communications leader with the judgment, range and industry experience to help SiriusXM tell a clear and compelling story, anchored around making SiriusXM the definitive home for audio content and fandom,” Greenstein said in a statement. “Jenny’s experience across entertainment, streaming, podcasting and advertising makes her the right leader to guide our communications into the next phase of SiriusXM’s strategy across our portfolio of audio businesses, and we’re thrilled to welcome her to the team.”

Tartikoff added, “SiriusXM brings together an extraordinary mix of brands, platforms, talent and technology, with a unique ability to connect fans with music, voices, stories and cultural moments they care about. As a longtime listener, I’ve experienced firsthand the thoughtful curation and authentic experiences SiriusXM creates, which makes joining the company especially meaningful. I’m excited to partner with the leadership team and communications organization to help shape and amplify the company’s story with purpose and impact.”
